incident: Fastpath stalled after UND_ERR_SOCKET while its Screen was attached.
findings: The running native process had stream_max_retries=0, so the first stream failure was terminal.
The cron watcher correctly declined to submit terminal input to an attached Screen.
Diagnostics recorded a non-terminal upstream socket failure after 631232 ms while receiving output; the remote cause is not established.
The earlier zero-retry workaround prevented repeated large-history retries but left attached sessions without automatic transport recovery.

repair.scope: Only the existing Fastpath native thread; other sessions were not reloaded.
repair.configuration: Private thread_recovery_overrides persisted and re-applied by the existing guarded Screen reloader.
repair.runtime: Existing latest checked-in bridge loaded by a graceful exact-thread reload; no runtime package update.

new_regressions: UND_ERR_SOCKET after a real shell side effect: one native retry includes the completed tool result and the side effect occurs exactly once.
Two consecutive UND_ERR_SOCKET failures stop at the configured single retry without duplicating the tool side effect.
An attached real Screen keeps its native goal active across a synthetic stream failure and executes a continuation tool without invoking the watcher.
validation.method: Installed Codex 0.164.0 and synthetic local inference endpoints. No injected failure in the user session.

limits: Remote socket closures cannot be prevented by the local bridge; recovery is bounded.
Earlier compaction reserves more room for partial reasoning but does not guarantee that arbitrary tool output fits.
The watcher still preserves attached terminals, pending drafts, user pauses, goal budgets and exhausted retry allowances.
Optional long-running real SDK tests were not rerun for this private configuration change.
